clue.text: Honour received by old German explorer

indicators.note: an honour received by someone is taken in, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: Hun is an old, derogatory name for a German
the DSO (Distinguished Service Order) is a British military honour

explanation.surface: A German explorer of old is being decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old German' is HUN, an old slang name, not an adjective on the explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Hudson was the English navigator who gave his name to Hudson Bay and the Hudson River.

clue.text: The film re-shown without a break

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other letters go around the article
re-shown means the film words are presented again in a different order

explanation.surface: A film is shown again from start to finish with no interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: 're-shown' rearranges THE FILM into HLFTIME, which wraps the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-time is the break between halves of a match.

clue.text: Despicable sorts feature prominently among old men

indicators.note: among places the starring piece within the old men

parts.note: old man is slang for father, so old men are dads
to star is to feature prominently

explanation.surface: Villains often turn up among elderly gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastards is an old word for cowardly, contemptible people.

clue.text: Slightly ahead? Tied after losing lead

indicators.note: losing its lead means the phrase drops its first letter

parts.note: done up means fastened or tied, as laces are

explanation.surface: A team slightly ahead is pegged back to a draw after losing the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied' reads as level scores, but it means fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: Being one-up is having a lead of a single point, so just in front.

clue.text: Nutter held bag containing ecstasy

indicators.note: the first word holds the drug inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: held means had, as in possessed
E is the usual slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
a case is a bag for carrying things

explanation.surface: A lunatic is caught carrying a bag with drugs in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a crazy person.

clue.text: Like some wines, European, said to contain grit

indicators.note: the word for said holds the courage inside it

parts.note: stated means said
bottle is British slang for courage, or grit

explanation.surface: A European is reputed to have plenty of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate-bottled wine is bottled at the vineyard where its grapes grew.

clue.text: Is it worn by a Parson Jack Russell?

definitions.text: Is it worn by a Parson Jack Russell?

parts.words: Is it worn by a Parson Jack Russell?
parts.note: the Parson Jack Russell is a terrier breed, so it might wear a dog's collar, while a parson wears a clerical collar

explanation.surface: A question about what a breed of terrier wears.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white band worn by clergy is nicknamed after the collar a dog wears.

clue.text: Fashion house providing mostly boring clothes for male

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the trimmed word dresses the male, holding it inside
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: arid means dull or boring
a man is a male

explanation.surface: A fashion label mostly sells dull menswear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb to dress, wrapping MAN in ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Armani is the Italian fashion label founded by Giorgio Armani.

clue.text: Name of palace in Cambridgeshire city, and description of it

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, in eastern England
Ely is the seat of a bishop, so it can be described as a see

explanation.surface: A palace in Ely and an account of what it looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is one, so 'description of it' gives SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elysee Palace in Paris is the French president's official residence.

clue.text: Attacked hooligan when he had burst in

indicators.note: the words burst into the hooligan, so they go inside that piece

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
he had shortens to he'd

explanation.surface: A thug arrived and started a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is a phrasal verb for striking out violently, so it means attacked.

clue.text: Drove in really tricky test, once

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A learner drove during a really hard driving test.
explanation.walkthrough: The O level was the British school exam taken at 16 until replaced by GCSEs in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary Level was the full name of that former British school examination, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Red wine good with a vegetable turnover

indicators.note: a turnover turns the vegetable over, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a yam is a starchy root vegetable

explanation.surface: A red wine goes well with a pastry turnover filled with vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like a pastry but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamay is the grape behind Beaujolais and the light red wine made from it.

clue.text: Leader of thieves reprimanded, being caught

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: rapped, as in rapped over the knuckles, means reprimanded

explanation.surface: The gang boss is told off after being arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapped and being caught both describe someone held fast with no escape.

clue.text: Defeat lightweight after little time? Right

indicators.note: the weight comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A boxer asks whether a lightweight beaten in no time is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to beat them heavily, a defeat.

clue.text: Hardly a bouncer where doctors gather socially?

definitions.meaning: a heavy weighted exercise ball, which barely bounces at all
a ball, or dance, held for members of the medical profession

explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a nightclub doorman, but here it means a ball that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy training ball is thrown, not bounced, and a doctors' dance would be a medicine ball.

clue.text: Church painters reforming group

parts.note: painters are artists

explanation.surface: Church painters set about reforming their circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a 19th-century British working-class movement campaigning for voting reform.
explanation.definitionFit: They were a political movement demanding parliamentary reform through the People's Charter.

clue.text: Well-read youngsters briefly absorbing Education Reform Act

indicators.note: absorbing means taking the other piece inside
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals
ERA is the initialism for the 1988 Education Reform Act in England

explanation.surface: Pupils who are well-read have taken in an education law.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means educated and well-read, as well as able to read.

clue.text: American statesman's honest policy ignored by English

parts.note: frank means honest and direct

indicators.note: the nationality is left out, so its letter drops from the policy word

parts.note: a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: An American politician's straight dealing is disregarded by the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Franklin was one of the founding fathers of the United States.

clue.text: Dog, one shouts, biting trainer viciously

indicators.note: the shouter bites into the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a crier, like a town crier, is one who shouts

indicators.note: viciously suggests the word is savaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A yapping dog bites its trainer savagely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one shouts' reads like a barking dog's action, but it names a person, the crier; 'viciously' scrambles the trainer's letters to AIRNTER for 'biting' to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The cairn terrier is a small Scottish terrier breed.

clue.text: Whisky drunk by companion about start of celebration

indicators.note: the drunkard goes about the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Whisky is drunk by a friend at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as a verb but is the noun, a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch is whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Key player at Lord's?

definitions.meaning: a key is something that unlocks, as a tin or bottle device does
Lord's is a London cricket ground, and a batter who begins the innings has this name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Key player' seems one phrase, a star of the team, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A key opens a lock, and in cricket the batter starting the innings is so named.

clue.text: Working coal pit, state-owned establishment

indicators.note: working the letters means kneading them into a new order

explanation.surface: A working coal mine owned by the state, as in nationalised industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like it describes the mine but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitol is the building where a US state legislature meets, an establishment belonging to the state.

clue.text: Stand made by Hannibal close to Mediterranean?

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the cannibal of The Silence of the Lambs

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The Carthaginian general Hannibal makes a stand near the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannibal' summons the general who fought Rome, but it is the film villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a reading stand for a speaker's notes or a Bible.

clue.text: Kick mongrel

definitions.meaning: in football, a kick of the ball from the wing into the centre
a dog of mixed breeds, a hybrid

explanation.definitionFit: A cross is both a football pass from the wing and an animal of mixed breeding.

clue.text: Nurses in East End sanatorium

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Nurses work in a sanatorium in London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse a patient is to tend them, look after them.

clue.text: Local dive re-established communication

indicators.note: re-established means set up again in a new form, so the letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood bar reopened after a closure.
explanation.definitionFit: A video call is a form of communication by live camera link.

clue.text: Shared out £2, the result of such aggressive marketing?

indicators.note: shared out means dealt around, so the letters are scattered and regrouped

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two pounds give two Ls

explanation.surface: Two pounds divided up is all a pushy sales pitch earns.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard sell is a high-pressure sales technique.

clue.text: A small seabird towards rear of ship

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A little seabird perches at the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical term for at or towards the back of a vessel.
